<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.
</app-context>

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.
</app-context>

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.
</app-context>

# OpenAI Whisper API (curl)

Transcribe an audio file via OpenAI’s `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint. Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` to use an OpenAI-compatible proxy or local gateway.

## Quick start

```bash
{baseDir}/scripts/transcribe.sh /path/to/audio.m4a
```

Defaults:

- Model: `whisper-1`
- Output: `<input>.txt`

## Useful flags

```bash
{baseDir}/scripts/transcribe.sh /path/to/audio.ogg --model whisper-1 --out /tmp/transcript.txt
{baseDir}/scripts/transcribe.sh /path/to/audio.m4a --language en
{baseDir}/scripts/transcribe.sh /path/to/audio.m4a --prompt "Speaker names: Peter, Daniel"
{baseDir}/scripts/transcribe.sh /path/to/audio.m4a --json --out /tmp/transcript.json
```

## API key

Set `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or configure it in the active OpenClaw config file (`$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, default `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`). Optionally set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` (for example `http://127.0.0.1:51805/v1`) to use an OpenAI-compatible proxy or local gateway:

```json5
{
  skills: {
    "openai-whisper-api": {
      apiKey: "OPENAI_KEY_HERE",
    },
  },
}
```

# Coding Agent (bash-first)

Use **bash** (with optional background mode) for all coding agent work. Simple and effective.

## ⚠️ PTY Mode: Codex/Pi/OpenCode yes, Claude Code no

For **Codex, Pi, and OpenCode**, PTY is still required (interactive terminal apps):

```bash
# ✅ Correct for Codex/Pi/OpenCode
bash pty:true command:"codex exec 'Your prompt'"
```

For **Claude Code** (`claude` CLI), use `--print --permission-mode bypassPermissions` instead.
`--dangerously-skip-permissions` with PTY can exit after the confirmation dialog.
`--print` mode keeps full tool access and avoids interactive confirmation:

```bash
# ✅ Correct for Claude Code (no PTY needed)
cd /path/to/project && claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --print 'Your task'

# For background execution: use background:true on the exec tool

# ❌ Wrong for Claude Code
bash pty:true command:"claude --dangerously-skip-permissions 'task'"
```

### Bash Tool Parameters

| Parameter    | Type    | Description                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `command`    | string  | The shell command to run                                                    |
| `pty`        | boolean | **Use for coding agents!** Allocates a pseudo-terminal for interactive CLIs |
| `workdir`    | string  | Working directory (agent sees only this folder's context)                   |
| `background` | boolean | Run in background, returns sessionId for monitoring                         |
| `timeout`    | number  | Timeout in seconds (kills process on expiry)                                |
| `elevated`   | boolean | Run on host instead of sandbox (if allowed)                                 |

### Process Tool Actions (for background sessions)

| Action      | Description                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `list`      | List all running/recent sessions                     |
| `poll`      | Check if session is still running                    |
| `log`       | Get session output (with optional offset/limit)      |
| `write`     | Send raw data to stdin                               |
| `submit`    | Send data + newline (like typing and pressing Enter) |
| `send-keys` | Send key tokens or hex bytes                         |
| `paste`     | Paste text (with optional bracketed mode)            |
| `kill`      | Terminate the session                                |

---

## Quick Start: One-Shot Tasks

For quick prompts/chats, create a temp git repo and run:

```bash
# Quick chat (Codex needs a git repo!)
SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d) && cd $SCRATCH && git init && codex exec "Your prompt here"

# Or in a real project - with PTY!
bash pty:true workdir:~/Projects/myproject command:"codex exec 'Add error handling to the API calls'"
```

**Why git init?** Codex refuses to run outside a trusted git directory. Creating a temp repo solves this for scratch work.

---

## The Pattern: workdir + background + pty

For longer tasks, use background mode with PTY:

```bash
# Start agent in target directory (with PTY!)
bash pty:true workdir:~/project background:true command:"codex exec --full-auto 'Build a snake game'"
# Returns sessionId for tracking

# Monitor progress
process action:log sessionId:XXX

# Check if done
process action:poll sessionId:XXX

# Send input (if agent asks a question)
process action:write sessionId:XXX data:"y"

# Submit with Enter (like typing "yes" and pressing Enter)
process action:submit sessionId:XXX data:"yes"

# Kill if needed
process action:kill sessionId:XXX
```

**Why workdir matters:** Agent wakes up in a focused directory, doesn't wander off reading unrelated files (like your soul.md 😅).

---

## Codex CLI

**Model:** `gpt-5.2-codex` is the default (set in ~/.codex/config.toml)

### Flags

| Flag            | Effect                                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |

# Coding Agent (bash-first)

Use **bash** (with optional background mode) for all coding agent work. Simple and effective.

## ⚠️ PTY Mode: Codex/Pi/OpenCode yes, Claude Code no

For **Codex, Pi, and OpenCode**, PTY is still required (interactive terminal apps):

```bash
# ✅ Correct for Codex/Pi/OpenCode
bash pty:true command:"codex exec 'Your prompt'"
```

For **Claude Code** (`claude` CLI), use `--print --permission-mode bypassPermissions` instead.
`--dangerously-skip-permissions` with PTY can exit after the confirmation dialog.
`--print` mode keeps full tool access and avoids interactive confirmation:

```bash
# ✅ Correct for Claude Code (no PTY needed)
cd /path/to/project && claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --print 'Your task'

# For background execution: use background:true on the exec tool

# ❌ Wrong for Claude Code
bash pty:true command:"claude --dangerously-skip-permissions 'task'"
```

### Bash Tool Parameters

| Parameter    | Type    | Description                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `command`    | string  | The shell command to run                                                    |
| `pty`        | boolean | **Use for coding agents!** Allocates a pseudo-terminal for interactive CLIs |
| `workdir`    | string  | Working directory (agent sees only this folder's context)                   |
| `background` | boolean | Run in background, returns sessionId for monitoring                         |
| `timeout`    | number  | Timeout in seconds (kills process on expiry)                                |
| `elevated`   | boolean | Run on host instead of sandbox (if allowed)                                 |

### Process Tool Actions (for background sessions)

| Action      | Description                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `list`      | List all running/recent sessions                     |
| `poll`      | Check if session is still running                    |
| `log`       | Get session output (with optional offset/limit)      |
| `write`     | Send raw data to stdin                               |
| `submit`    | Send data + newline (like typing and pressing Enter) |
| `send-keys` | Send key tokens or hex bytes                         |
| `paste`     | Paste text (with optional bracketed mode)            |
| `kill`      | Terminate the session                                |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat >&2 <<'EOF'
Usage:
  transcribe.sh <audio-file> [--model whisper-1] [--out /path/to/out.txt] [--language en] [--prompt "hint"] [--json]
EOF
  exit 2
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "" || "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
fi

in="${1:-}"
shift || true

model="whisper-1"
out=""
language=""
prompt=""
response_format="text"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --model)
      model="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --out)
      out="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --language)
      language="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --prompt)
      prompt="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --json)
      response_format="json"
      shift 1
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown arg: $1" >&2
      usage
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ ! -f "$in" ]]; then
  echo "File not found: $in" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ "${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}" == "" ]]; then
  echo "Missing OPENAI_API_KEY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ "$out" == "" ]]; then
  base="${in%.*}"
  if [[ "$response_format" == "json" ]]; then
    out="${base}.json"
  else
    out="${base}.txt"
  fi
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"

api_base="${OPENAI_BASE_URL:-https://api.openai.com/v1}"
api_base="${api_base%/}"

curl -sS "${api_base}/audio/transcriptions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -F "file=@${in}" \
  -F "model=${model}" \
  -F "response_format=${response_format}" \
  ${language:+-F "language=${language}"} \
  ${prompt:+-F "prompt=${prompt}"} \
  >"$out"

echo "$out"

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.

payload.message: 在git上搜索moss-tts-nano的语音模型并分析其功能
我先去 GitHub 和公开资料里确认 `moss-tts-nano` 的仓库来源、模型定位和实际能力，再给你一个简明分析。

content.text: 我先去 GitHub 和公开资料里确认 `moss-tts-nano` 的仓库来源、模型定位和实际能力，再给你一个简明分析。

payload.message:
GitHub 上我查到的目标仓库是：

- [OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)
- 同系列总仓库：[OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS)

**它是什么**
`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 是一个开源的**超小型多语言 TTS 模型**，主打“**CPU 可跑、实时生成、轻量部署**”。仓库说明写明它只有 **0.1B 参数**，定位是本地 demo、轻量服务和产品集成，而不是追求最高音质的大模型。来源：GitHub README  
[OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)

**核心功能**
- **文本转语音**
  输入文本，输出语音 wav。
- **语音克隆**
  用一段参考音频作为 `prompt-audio-path` / `prompt-speech`，生成同音色的新语音。
- **多语言**
  README 列出支持 20 种语言，包括中英日德法韩俄阿拉伯语等。  
  来源：[MOSS-TTS-Nano README](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)
- **流式推理**
  强调低首包延迟和实时流式生成。
- **CPU 友好**
  官方写明可在 **4 核 CPU** 上运行；后续还发布了 **ONNX CPU 版**，号称比原版推理效率接近提升 2 倍。  
  来源：[MOSS-TTS-Nano README](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)
- **本地 Web Demo**
  可运行 `app.py` 或 `app_onnx.py` 提供浏览器界面。
- **CLI**
  提供 `moss-tts-nano generate` 和 `moss-tts-nano serve` 两类命令。
- **微调**
  仓库已放出 finetuning 代码。

**技术特点**
- 架构是 **Audio Tokenizer + LLM 的纯自回归管线**
- 原生音频格式强调 **48 kHz、双声道**
- 搭配 `MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano` 作为音频 tokenizer/backbone  
来源：[MOSS-TTS-Nano README](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)

**适合什么场景**
- 本地语音播报
- 浏览器朗读
- 轻量语音助手
- 多语言配音 demo
- CPU-only 设备上的 TTS 服务
- 低资源产品原型

**不适合什么**
- 它是 **TTS，不是 STT**，不能做语音识别
- 不是家族里音质最强的旗舰模型
- 复杂情感、超高保真、长对话表现，通常还是大模型系列更强  
参考家族说明：[OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS)

**一句话判断**
如果你要的是“**能在本地轻量跑起来的多语言语音合成/音色克隆模型**”，`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 很值得看；如果你要“最强音质/复杂表达”，它更像部署友好的 nano 版本，而不是旗舰版本。

如果你要，我下一步可以继续帮你：
1. 分析它是否适合你现在这台 Mac 本地部署
2. 对比 `MOSS-TTS-Nano` 和 `ChatTTS` / `CosyVoice` / `F5-TTS`
3. 直接给你整理一份安装路线图

```bash

```

例如在项目目录里：

```bash
cd /path/to/project
claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --print "分析这个仓库的认证流程"
```

你也可以在 `Codex` 里让代理帮你执行这个命令，等于“用 Codex 调 Claude Code”。

常见接法有 3 种：

1. 直接命令行调用  
   最简单，Codex 和 Claude Code 各跑各的，Codex 负责调度。

2. 写一个包装脚本  
   比如建个 `run-claude.sh`：

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cd "$1" || exit 1
shift
claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --print "$*"
```

然后用：
```bash
./run-claude.sh /path/to/project "重构这个模块"
```

3. 在工作流里混用  
   用 Codex 做主代理，某些任务转交给 Claude Code CLI，比如：
   - Codex 负责改代码
   - Claude Code 负责大范围审查/重构建议
   - 最后再回到 Codex 落地修改

  - 游戏循环

`build-game`

一台英伟达T4主机；如何使用本地模型管理多agent龙虾；给出方案

可以做，但一台 T4 要把思路放对：**不要给每个 agent 单独加载一个大模型**，而是用一个本地 OpenAI-compatible 模型服务作为“共享大脑”，Lobster/ClawFlow 负责编排多个 agent 的任务、状态、审批和恢复。

**推荐架构**
```text
User / OpenClaw
   |
   v
Lobster 工作流层
   |
   |-- Planner Agent
   |-- Coder Agent
   |-- Reviewer Agent
   |-- Tool/Deploy Agent
   |
   v
本地模型服务 OpenAI-compatible API
   |
   v
NVIDIA T4 16GB
```

Lobster 的定位不是“模型”，而是**确定性工作流外壳**：负责步骤编排、审批、恢复 token、工具调用。真正的推理统一走本地模型 API。

**T4 模型选择**
T4 通常是 16GB VRAM，不适合同时跑多个大模型。建议：

- 通用任务：`Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` 或 `Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-AWQ`
- 代码任务：`Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct` 或 `Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-AWQ`
- 如果追求中文和代码平衡：优先 `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-AWQ`
- 如果想更省显存：用 `GGUF Q4_K_M` 量化模型，通过 `llama.cpp` 或 `Ollama`
- 如果想更像服务端：用 `vLLM + AWQ/GPTQ`，提供 OpenAI-compatible API

一台 T4 上最稳的策略是：**只常驻一个 7B/14B 量化模型**，多 agent 共享它，通过不同 system prompt 区分角色。

**模型服务方案**
优先级我建议这样选：

1. `vLLM`
适合你要做多 agent 并发、队列、OpenAI API 兼容。
示例：
```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-AWQ \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
```

2. `Ollama`
适合快速落地、管理模型简单。
示例：
```bash
ollama run qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

3. `llama.cpp`
适合极致省显存和 GGUF 量化。
示例：
```bash
llama-server \
  -m /models/qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  -c 8192
```

**OpenClaw 接本地模型**
把本地服务伪装成 OpenAI API：

```bash
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="local-anything"
export OPENAI_MODEL="Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-AWQ"
```

如果你自己的后端也走 OpenAI-compatible provider，就同样配置：

```bash
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
OPENAI_API_KEY=local-anything
OPENAI_MODEL=Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-AWQ
GENERATION_PROVIDER_ORDER=openai,codex-cli
```

**Lobster 多 Agent 编排方式**
建议把多 agent 设计成“同模型，不同角色，不同步骤”。

例如一个代码任务：

```yaml
name: local-multi-agent-coding
args:
  task:
    default: "Implement feature"

steps:
  - id: plan
    command: local-agent planner --json
    env:
      ROLE: "Planner"
      MODEL_BASE_URL: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1"

  - id: code
    command: local-agent coder --json
    stdin: $plan.stdout
    env:
      ROLE: "Coder"

  - id: review
    command: local-agent reviewer --json
    stdin: $code.stdout
    env:
      ROLE: "Reviewer"

  - id: approve
    command: local-agent summarize-change --json
    stdin: $review.stdout
    approval: required

  - id: apply
    command: local-agent apply --execute
    stdin: $review.stdout
    condition: $approve.approved
```

这里的 `local-agent` 可以是你写的一个小 CLI：接收 role、prompt、stdin，然后调用本地 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions`。

**Agent 角色建议**
一台 T4 不适合跑太多并发，建议 4 个以内：

- `Planner Agent`：拆任务、生成步骤、判断风险
- `Builder/Coder Agent`：执行实现
- `Reviewer Agent`：检查 bug、安全、测试缺口
- `Tool Agent`：调用外部工具、部署、上传、跑测试

如果做游戏/产品生成，可以换成：

- `PM Agent`：需求和验收标准
- `Design Agent`：UI/UX 风格
- `Game Agent`：玩法和代码
- `QA Agent`：移动端、性能、可玩性测试

**关键限制**
一台 T4 的瓶颈不是 agent 数量，而是模型推理吞吐。建议：

- 并发 agent 控制在 `1-3`
- 大任务走队列，不要全部同时请求
- 上下文控制在 `8k` 或 `16k`，别一上来拉满
- 长文档用 RAG，不要全部塞进 prompt
- 用一个强一点的 7B/14B 量化模型，比多个小模型更稳定
- 审批、部署、写文件这类副作用必须放 Lobster approval gate

**推荐落地路线**
1. T4 主机安装 `vLLM` 或 `Ollama`。
2. 先跑一个 `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-AWQ`。
3. 暴露 `OpenAI-compatible API`：`http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`。
4. OpenClaw/后端统一配置 `OPENAI_BASE_URL` 指向本地。
5. 写一个 `local-agent` CLI，封装不同 role 的 prompt。
6. 用 Lobster `.lobster` 文件编排 planner/coder/reviewer/approval/apply。
7. 后续再加 Redis/SQLite task queue 和日志审计。

我的建议是先别追求“很多 agent 同时跑”，先做成：**一个本地模型服务 + Lobster 工作流 + 4 个角色 agent + 严格审批**。这套在 T4 上最稳，也最容易扩展。
不需要代码建议；用本地7B模型进行管理，多个使用线上API的龙虾

可以，思路应该反过来：**本地 7B 不负责干重活，只负责“管理和调度”；真正执行复杂任务的多个 Lobster/agent 走线上 API。**

你的目标架构可以这样设计：

```text
本地 7B Manager
   |
   | 判断任务类型
   | 拆分任务
   | 分配给不同 Lobster
   | 监控状态
   | 汇总结果
   v
多个线上 API Lobster / Agent Worker
   |
   |-- Research Lobster    -> Claude / OpenAI / Gemini API
   |-- Coding Lobster      -> Claude Code / Codex / OpenAI API
   |-- UI Lobster          -> v0 / Figma / GPT-4.1 / Claude
   |-- Game Lobster        -> build-game / game-engine / image/video API
   |-- Deploy Lobster      -> Vercel / Railway / GitHub API
   |-- QA Lobster          -> browser test / review / debug API
```

**核心定位**
本地 7B 模型只做：

- 任务分类
- agent 路由
- prompt 改写
- 成本控制
- 优先级排序
- 状态追踪
- 结果汇总
- 决定是否需要人工审批

不要让本地 7B 做：

- 大型代码生成
- 深度研究
- 复杂推理
- 多模态生成
- 长上下文总结
- 关键质量审查

这些交给线上 API Lobster。

**为什么这样适合 T4**
T4 跑 7B 很稳，做 manager 足够：

- 7B 模型延迟低
- 成本为零或接近零
- 可以一直常驻
- 不需要太强推理，只需要稳定路由
- 线上 API 只在真正需要时调用，省钱

本地 7B 的最佳角色是“项目经理/调度器”，不是“专家执行者”。

**Manager 的决策模型**
每个用户请求先让本地 7B 输出一个结构化决策：

```json
{
  "intent": "build_game",
  "complexity": "medium",
  "required_agents": ["pm", "game", "ui", "qa", "deploy"],
  "online_api_needed": true,
  "approval_required": true,
  "budget_level": "normal",
  "steps": [
    "clarify_requirement",
    "generate_game",
    "review_mobile_playability",
    "publish_to_aigames"
  ]
}
```

然后 Lobster 根据这个 JSON 去调不同线上 worker。

**多个 Lobster 的分工**
我建议拆成这些垂类 Lobster：

1. `pm-lobster`
负责：
- 需求理解
- PRD
- 用户故事
- 验收标准
- scope 控制

适合接：
- OpenAI API
- Claude API
- 你已装的 `product-manager` skill

2. `ui-lobster`
负责：
- UI 风格
- H5 页面视觉
- 设计系统
- 移动端布局

适合接：
- Claude
- OpenAI
- v0
- Figma AI
- 你已装的 `ui-designer` skill

3. `game-lobster`
负责：
- H5 游戏生成
- 3D 游戏 demo
- 玩法循环
- 移动端控制

适合接：
- build-game
- game-engine
- Claude / OpenAI API
- 你已装的 `build-game`、`game-engine`

4. `qa-lobster`
负责：
- 找 bug
- 移动端体验检查
- 性能风险
- 可玩性分析

适合接：
- OpenAI / Claude
- 浏览器测试工具
- 本地截图/日志工具

5. `deploy-lobster`
负责：

GitHub 上我查到的目标仓库是：

- 同系列总仓库：[OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS)

**它是什么**
`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 是一个开源的**超小型多语言 TTS 模型**，主打“**CPU 可跑、实时生成、轻量部署**”。仓库说明写明它只有 **0.1B 参数**，定位是本地 demo、轻量服务和产品集成，而不是追求最高音质的大模型。来源：GitHub README  
[OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)

**核心功能**
- **文本转语音**
  输入文本，输出语音 wav。
- **语音克隆**
  用一段参考音频作为 `prompt-audio-path` / `prompt-speech`，生成同音色的新语音。
- **多语言**
  README 列出支持 20 种语言，包括中英日德法韩俄阿拉伯语等。  
  来源：[MOSS-TTS-Nano README](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)
- **流式推理**
  强调低首包延迟和实时流式生成。
- **CPU 友好**
  官方写明可在 **4 核 CPU** 上运行；后续还发布了 **ONNX CPU 版**，号称比原版推理效率接近提升 2 倍。  
  来源：[MOSS-TTS-Nano README](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)
- **本地 Web Demo**
  可运行 `app.py` 或 `app_onnx.py` 提供浏览器界面。
- **CLI**
  提供 `moss-tts-nano generate` 和 `moss-tts-nano serve` 两类命令。
- **微调**
  仓库已放出 finetuning 代码。

**技术特点**
- 架构是 **Audio Tokenizer + LLM 的纯自回归管线**
- 原生音频格式强调 **48 kHz、双声道**
- 搭配 `MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano` 作为音频 tokenizer/backbone  
来源：[MOSS-TTS-Nano README](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano)

**适合什么场景**
- 本地语音播报
- 浏览器朗读
- 轻量语音助手
- 多语言配音 demo
- CPU-only 设备上的 TTS 服务
- 低资源产品原型

**不适合什么**
- 它是 **TTS，不是 STT**，不能做语音识别
- 不是家族里音质最强的旗舰模型
- 复杂情感、超高保真、长对话表现，通常还是大模型系列更强  
参考家族说明：[OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS)

**一句话判断**
如果你要的是“**能在本地轻量跑起来的多语言语音合成/音色克隆模型**”，`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 很值得看；如果你要“最强音质/复杂表达”，它更像部署友好的 nano 版本，而不是旗舰版本。

按我刚才给的 `1` 来分析：**`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 是否适合你现在这台 Mac 本地部署。**

先说结论：**可以作为本地语音播报模块考虑，但不适合解决你当前“语音输入转写给 Codex”这个核心问题。**  
原因很关键：`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 是 **TTS（文本转语音）**，不是 **STT（语音转文字）**。

结合你当前环境来看：

- 你现在的主目标是：`Neomix-39A4 -> 采集音频 -> 转写 -> 确认 -> Codex`
- 这个链路最缺的是 **本地 STT**
- `MOSS-TTS-Nano` 解决的是反方向：
  - `文本 -> 语音播报`
  - 不解决 `语音 -> 文本`

所以如果问“能不能装”：
- 大概率能部署
- 它主打轻量、CPU 可跑，对本地 Mac 比较友好
- 作为后续“Codex 回答后，用本地语音读出来”的模块，方向是对的

但如果问“适不适合现在优先接”：
- **不适合优先做**
- 因为它不能替代 Whisper/faster-whisper
- 装完以后，你的语音闭环还是卡在“听不懂用户说话”

更准确地说，它适合放在你的链路后半段：

```text
用户说话
-> 本地 STT
-> Codex 执行
-> Codex 返回文本
-> MOSS-TTS-Nano 朗读结果
```

所以它的最佳定位是：
- 本地语音播报
- 中文/多语言朗读
- 轻量语音助手输出层
- 给你的 HTML 页面补一个“播报 Codex 结果”的能力

不适合的定位是：
- 麦克风识别
- 音频转写
- 替代 Whisper

我的建议顺序是：

1. 先把本地 `STT` 装通  
2. 跑通 `录音 -> 转写 -> Codex`
3. 再考虑接 `MOSS-TTS-Nano` 做结果播报

如果你愿意，我下一步可以继续帮你做 `分析2`：把 `MOSS-TTS-Nano` 和 `ChatTTS / CosyVoice / F5-TTS` 做一版简明对比。

  <style>
    :root {

    * { box-sizing: border-box; }

    body {
      min-height: 100svh;
      margin: 0;
      color: var(--ink);
      font-family: var(--sans);
      background:
        radial-gradient(circle at 18% 8%, rgba(199, 122, 45, 0.18), transparent 28rem),
        radial-gradient(circle at 90% 10%, rgba(85, 114, 94, 0.14), transparent 24rem),
        var(--bg);
    }

    button, textarea {
      font: inherit;
    }

    .shell {
      width: min(1440px, calc(100vw - 36px));
      margin: 0 auto;
      padding: 26px 0 34px;
    }

    .topbar {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: space-between;
      gap: 20px;
      padding-bottom: 22px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
    }

    .brand-kicker {
      margin: 0 0 8px;
      color: var(--muted);
      font-family: var(--mono);
      font-size: 12px;
      letter-spacing: 0.08em;
      text-transform: uppercase;
    }

    h1 {
      margin: 0;
      font-size: clamp(34px, 5.7vw, 76px);
      line-height: 0.92;
      letter-spacing: -0.075em;
    }

    .system-pill {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 10px;
      min-height: 46px;
      padding: 0 16px;
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: 999px;
      background: var(--paper);
      color: var(--muted);
      box-shadow: var(--shadow);
      white-space: nowrap;
    }

    .dot {
      width: 10px;
      height: 10px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      background: var(--green);
      box-shadow: 0 0 0 7px rgba(85, 114, 94, 0.14);
    }

    .layout {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 330px minmax(440px, 1fr) 360px;
      gap: 18px;
      margin-top: 22px;
    }

    .panel {
      min-height: 670px;
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: var(--radius);
      background: rgba(255, 253, 248, 0.82);
      box-shadow: var(--shadow);
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .panel-inner {
      padding: 22px;
    }

    .label {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: space-between;
      gap: 12px;
      margin-bottom: 20px;
      color: var(--muted);
      font-family: var(--mono);
      font-size: 12px;
      text-transform: uppercase;
    }

    .device-hero {
      padding: 20px;
      border-radius: 26px;
      background: var(--dark);
      color: white;
    }

    .device-hero h2 {
      margin: 0 0 8px;
      font-size: 30px;
      letter-spacing: -0.06em;
    }

    .device-hero p {
      margin: 0;
      color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.66);
      line-height: 1.5;
    }

    .device-visual {
      height: 190px;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      margin: 18px 0;
      border-radius: 28px;
      background:
        linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(25, 24, 23, 0.06) 1px, transparent 1px),
        linear-gradient(rgba(25, 24, 23, 0.06) 1px, transparent 1px),
        var(--soft);
      background-size: 28px 28px;
    }

    .mic {
      position: relative;
      width: 90px;
      height: 128px;
      border-radius: 48px 48px 36px 36px;
      background: linear-gradient(180deg, #3c3933, #171614);
      box-shadow: 0 22px 48px rgba(25, 24, 23, 0.24);
    }

    .mic::before {
      content: "";
      position: absolute;
      left: 50%;
      bottom: -34px;
      width: 56px;
      height: 30px;
      border: 8px solid var(--dark);
      border-top: 0;
      border-radius: 0 0 30px 30px;
      transform: translateX(-50%);
    }

    .mic::after {
      content: "";
      position: absolute;
      inset: 18px 22px auto;
      height: 52px;
      border-top: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.26);
      border-bottom: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.20);
    }

    .stat-list {
      display: grid;
      gap: 10px;
    }

    .stat {
      display: flex;
      justify-content: space-between;
      gap: 14px;
      padding: 13px 0;
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
      color: var(--muted);
      font-size: 14px;
    }

    .stat strong {
      color: var(--ink);
      font-family: var(--mono);
      font-size: 12px;
      text-align: right;
    }

    .stage {
      min-height: 670px;
      padding: 22px;
    }

    .record-area {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 280px;
      gap: 16px;
      align-items: stretch;
    }

    .transcript {
      min-height: 282px;
      padding: 22px;
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: 30px;
      background: var(--paper);
    }

    .transcript h2 {
      margin: 0 0 14px;
      font-size: 34px;
      letter-spacing: -0.06em;
    }

    textarea {
      width: 100%;

      border-radius: 22px;
      outline: none;
      background: var(--soft);
      color: var(--ink);
      line-height: 1.45;
    }

    textarea:focus {
      border-color: var(--accent);
      background: #fff;
    }

import subprocess, textwrap, tempfile, os
code = r'''
import CoreAudio

def get(prop_sel, obj, addr_scope=CoreAudio.kAudioObjectPropertyScopeGlobal):
    addr = CoreAudio.AudioObjectPropertyAddress()
    addr.mSelector = prop_sel
    addr.mScope = addr_scope
    addr.mElement = CoreAudio.kAudioObjectPropertyElementMain
    sz = CoreAudio.UInt32()
    CoreAudio.AudioObjectGetPropertyDataSize(obj, addr, 0, None, sz)
    buf = (CoreAudio.c_byte * sz.value)()
    CoreAudio.AudioObjectGetPropertyData(obj, addr, 0, None, sz, buf)
    return bytes(buf)

system = CoreAudio.AudioObjectID(CoreAudio.kAudioObjectSystemObject)
addr = CoreAudio.AudioObjectPropertyAddress()
addr.mSelector = CoreAudio.kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices
addr.mScope = CoreAudio.kAudioObjectPropertyScopeGlobal
addr.mElement = CoreAudio.kAudioObjectPropertyElementMain
sz = CoreAudio.UInt32()
CoreAudio.AudioObjectGetPropertyDataSize(system, addr, 0, None, sz)
count = sz.value // CoreAudio.sizeof(CoreAudio.AudioObjectID)
arr = (CoreAudio.AudioObjectID * count)()
CoreAudio.AudioObjectGetPropertyData(system, addr, 0, None, sz, arr)

for dev in arr:
    try:
        name_b = get(CoreAudio.kAudioObjectPropertyName, dev)
        uid_b = get(CoreAudio.kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceUID, dev)
        name = name_b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore').strip('\x00')
        uid = uid_b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore').strip('\x00')
        in_streams = len(get(CoreAudio.kAudioDevicePropertyStreams, dev, CoreAudio.kAudioDevicePropertyScopeInput)) // CoreAudio.sizeof(CoreAudio.AudioStreamID)
        out_streams = len(get(CoreAudio.kAudioDevicePropertyStreams, dev, CoreAudio.kAudioDevicePropertyScopeOutput)) // CoreAudio.sizeof(CoreAudio.AudioStreamID)
        print(f'id={int(dev)} name={name} uid={uid} inputs={in_streams} outputs={out_streams}')
    except Exception as e:
        pass
'''
fd, p = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.swift')
os.write(fd, code.encode())
os.close(fd)
subprocess.run(['swift', p], check=False)
os.unlink(p)

- You add structure only when the task calls for it. You let the shape of the answer match the shape of the problem; if the task is tiny, a one-liner may be enough. Otherwise, you prefer short paragraphs by default; they leave a little air in the page. You order sections from general to specific to supporting detail.

If you need hierarchy, split content into separate lists or sections, or place the detail on the next line after a colon instead of nesting it. For numbered lists, use only the `1. 2. 3.` style, never `1)`. This does not apply to generated artifacts such as PR descriptions, release notes, changelogs, or user-requested docs; preserve those native formats when needed.

payload.message: 本地stt是什么系统

现在本地 STT 用的是 **faster-whisper 系统**。

具体来说：

- STT 类型：`Whisper` 本地语音识别
- 推理框架：`faster-whisper`
- 运行位置：本机项目虚拟环境 [`.venv-stt`](/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/.venv-stt)
- 调用脚本：[local-stt.py](/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/tools/local-stt.py)
- 默认模型目录：[faster-whisper-base](/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/models/faster-whisper-base)
- bridge 接口：`http://127.0.0.1:18889/transcribe`

当前链路是：

```text
Neomix-39A4 麦克风
-> 浏览器采集音频
-> 本地 bridge
-> local-stt.py
-> faster-whisper
-> 返回转写文字
-> 页面显示
-> 用户确认后交给 Codex
```

也就是说，它已经不依赖 OpenAI Whisper API 额度了，转写是在你本机完成的。

### CLI Command: `moss-tts-nano generate`

After `pip install -e .`, you can call the packaged CLI directly:

```bash
moss-tts-nano generate \
  --prompt-speech assets/audio/zh_1.wav \
```

For the ONNX CPU backend, add `--backend onnx`:

```bash
moss-tts-nano generate \
  --backend onnx \
  --prompt-speech assets/audio/zh_1.wav \
  --text "欢迎关注模思智能、上海创智学院与复旦大学自然语言处理实验室。"
```

Useful notes:

- `moss-tts-nano generate` writes to `generated_audio/moss_tts_nano_output.wav` by default.
- `--prompt-speech` is the friendly alias for the reference audio path used by voice cloning.
- `--text-file` is supported for long-form synthesis.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Sequence

from onnx_tts_runtime import (
    DEFAULT_BROWSER_ONNX_MODEL_DIR,
    DEFAULT_BROWSER_ONNX_OUTPUT_PATH,
    OnnxTtsRuntime,
)


def set_logging() -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s",
        level=logging.INFO,
    )


def parse_args(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run native onnxruntime CPU inference on browser_onnx exported assets.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model-dir",
        default=None,
        help=(
            "browser_onnx model directory. If omitted, the script uses "
            f"{DEFAULT_BROWSER_ONNX_MODEL_DIR} and auto-downloads the ONNX assets on first run."
        ),
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-audio-path",
        default=str(DEFAULT_BROWSER_ONNX_OUTPUT_PATH),
        help="Where to save the generated waveform.",
    )
    text_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    text_group.add_argument("--text", help="Text to synthesize.")
    text_group.add_argument("--text-file", help="Path to a UTF-8 text file to synthesize.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--voice",
        default="Junhao",
        help="Built-in voice preset name used only when no reference audio path is provided.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--prompt-audio-path",
        "--reference-audio-path",
        dest="prompt_audio_path",
        default=None,
        help="Local reference audio path used directly for voice cloning. When provided, it overrides --voice.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--sample-mode",
        choices=("greedy", "fixed", "full"),
        default="fixed",
        help="greedy=do_sample false, fixed=fixed hyperparameter sampled frame, full=host sampled full frame.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--do-sample",
        type=int,
        nargs="?",
        const=1,
        default=1,
        choices=[0, 1],
        help="Whether to sample. If 0, sample_mode is forced to greedy.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--realtime-streaming-decode",
        type=int,
        nargs="?",
        const=1,
        default=1,
        choices=[0, 1],
        help="Use codec streaming decode path internally instead of full decode.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--cpu-threads", type=int, default=4, help="onnxruntime intra-op thread count.")
    parser.add_argument("--max-new-frames", type=int, default=375, help="Maximum generated audio frames.")
    parser.add_argument("--voice-clone-max-text-tokens", type=int, default=75, help="Chunk long text by token budget.")
    parser.add_argument("--text-temperature", type=float, default=1.0, help="Text-layer sampling temperature.")
    parser.add_argument("--text-top-p", type=float, default=1.0, help="Text-layer top-p sampling.")
    parser.add_argument("--text-top-k", type=int, default=50, help="Text-layer top-k sampling.")
    parser.add_argument("--audio-temperature", type=float, default=0.8, help="Audio-layer sampling temperature.")
    parser.add_argument("--audio-top-p", type=float, default=0.95, help="Audio-layer top-p sampling.")
    parser.add_argument("--audio-top-k", type=int, default=25, help="Audio-layer top-k sampling.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--audio-repetition-penalty",
        type=float,
        default=1.2,
        help="Audio-layer repetition penalty.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--enable-wetext-processing",
        type=int,
        nargs="?",
        const=1,
        default=1,
        choices=[0, 1],
        help="Enable WeTextProcessing text normalization before inference.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--disable-wetext-processing",
        action="store_true",
        help="Disable WeTextProcessing even if enabled above.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--enable-normalize-tts-text",
        dest="enable_normalize_tts_text",
        action="store_true",
        default=True,
        help="Enable normalize_tts_text robust cleanup before inference.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--disable-normalize-tts-text",
        dest="disable_normalize_tts_text",
        action="store_true",
        help="Disable normalize_tts_text robust cleanup before inference.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=None, help="Optional random seed.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--print-voice-clone-text-chunks",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print the effective chunked text before synthesis.",
    )
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def resolve_text(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    if args.text is not None:
        return str(args.text)
    return Path(args.text_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def maybe_print_voice_clone_text_chunks(runtime: OnnxTtsRuntime, text: str, max_tokens: int) -> None:
    chunks = runtime.split_voice_clone_text(text, max_tokens=max_tokens)
    effective_chunks = chunks if len(chunks) > 1 else [text]
    print("Voice clone text chunks")
    print("----------------------")
    print(f"max_tokens={max_tokens} chunks={len(effective_chunks)}")
    for chunk_index, chunk_text in enumerate(effective_chunks, start=1):
        print(f"[chunk {chunk_index}]")

import argparse
from typing import Optional, Sequence

from moss_tts_nano.defaults import (
    DEFAULT_AUDIO_TOKENIZER_PATH,
    DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_PATH,
    DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR,
)


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="moss-tts-nano",
        description="Command line interface for MOSS-TTS-Nano.",
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    generate_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "generate",
        help="Generate audio by forwarding to infer.py.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--backend",
        default="pytorch",
        choices=("pytorch", "onnx"),
        help="Inference backend to use.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--checkpoint",
        default=str(DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_PATH),
        help="PyTorch backend only. MOSS-TTS-Nano checkpoint source. Can be a HF repo id or local directory.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--audio-tokenizer",
        "--audio_tokenizer",
        dest="audio_tokenizer",
        default=str(DEFAULT_AUDIO_TOKENIZER_PATH),
        help="PyTorch backend only. MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano source. Can be a HF repo id or local directory.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--onnx-model-dir",
        default=None,
        help="ONNX backend only. browser_onnx model directory. Defaults to the repo's auto-download location.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        "--output-audio-path",
        dest="output_audio_path",
        default=str(DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR / "moss_tts_nano_output.wav"),
        help="Output wav path.",
    )
    text_group = generate_parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    text_group.add_argument("--text", help="Text to synthesize.")
    text_group.add_argument("--text-file", help="Path to a UTF-8 text file to synthesize.")
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        default="voice_clone",
        choices=("voice_clone", "continuation"),
        help="Inference mode.",

    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--prompt-speech",
        "--prompt_speech",
        "--prompt-audio-path",
        dest="prompt_audio_path",
        default=None,
        help="Reference speech used for voice cloning.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(
        "--prompt-text",
        default=None,
        help="PyTorch backend only. Reference transcript used by continuation mode.",
    )
    generate_parser.add_argument(

content.text: moss语音角色的音色如何调整，比如女声

payload.message: moss语音角色的音色如何调整，比如女声

`MOSS-TTS-Nano` 调音色主要有两种方式：

**1. 用内置 voice preset**
你刚才测试用的是：

```bash
--voice Junhao
```

这是内置声音预设。要换女声，就需要换成仓库支持的 female voice 名称。当前 README 只示例了 `Junhao`，没有在文档里完整列出所有 preset 名，所以最稳的做法是从模型 manifest 里查可用 voice 列表。

可以先查：

```bash
rg -n "voice|speaker|Junhao|female|女" /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/third_party/MOSS-TTS-Nano/models
```

找到可用名字后这样生成：

```bash
/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/.venv-moss-tts/bin/moss-tts-nano generate \
  --backend onnx \
  --voice 女声预设名 \
  --text '你好，又是美好的一天。' \
  --output /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/tmp/moss-tts-female.wav
```

**2. 用参考音频做音色克隆**
这是更可靠的女声方案。准备一段女声参考音频，比如 `female_ref.wav`，然后：

```bash
/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/.venv-moss-tts/bin/moss-tts-nano generate \
  --backend onnx \
  --prompt-speech /path/to/female_ref.wav \
  --text '你好，又是美好的一天。' \
  --output /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/aigame/tmp/moss-tts-female.wav
```

这种方式会尽量模仿参考音频的音色，比猜内置 preset 更可控。

简单建议：
- 只是快速换声音：先找 `--voice` preset
- 想要稳定女声：用 `--prompt-speech` 女声参考音频做 voice clone

我建议下一步直接帮你查当前本机模型里的可用 voice preset，然后找一个女声测试生成。

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}
</app-context>

payload.message: 语音转文本有哪些好用的方案

语音转文本（STT）我建议按“本地、云端、实时性”来选。你现在已经跑通的方案是 **本地 faster-whisper**，属于最稳的本地路线之一。

**本地方案**
- `faster-whisper`
  适合你当前项目。优点是本地运行、无需 API 额度、速度比原版 Whisper 好，支持中文。你现在用的就是它。
- `whisper.cpp`
  适合极轻量部署，CPU 跑得稳，Mac/小主机/边缘设备很好用。缺点是接入时要处理模型格式和命令行调用。
- `mlx-whisper`
  适合 Apple Silicon Mac，本地速度很好，能用 Apple 的 MLX 框架。缺点是更偏 Mac，跨平台一般。
- `FunASR / SenseVoice`
  中文场景很强，尤其普通话、多语种、口语转写、标点等体验不错。适合中文优先的语音助手。
- `Vosk`
  离线、轻量、低资源。准确率不如 Whisper/SenseVoice，但适合简单命令词、弱网、老设备。

**云端方案**
- `OpenAI Whisper API`
  准确、接入简单，但要额度和网络。你之前已经测试过，链路通，只是当前 OpenAI 额度不足。
- `AssemblyAI`
  英文和会议场景成熟，有说话人分离、摘要等功能。
- `Deepgram`
  实时转写很强，适合语音通话、客服、低延迟场景。
- `Google Speech-to-Text`
  传统企业级，语言覆盖广，稳定但配置偏重。
- `Azure Speech`
  适合企业、微软生态、实时字幕、会议类。
- `科大讯飞 / 阿里云 / 腾讯云 ASR`
  中文商业场景强，适合国内网络和普通话识别。

**按你的项目推荐**
你的目标是：

```text
Neomix 麦克风
-> 浏览器录音
-> STT 转文字
-> Codex 执行
-> MOSS-TTS-Nano 朗读
```

我建议优先级是：

1. `faster-whisper`
当前已经装好，继续作为默认本地 STT。

2. `SenseVoice / FunASR`
作为中文增强备用方案，适合你后续想提高中文口语识别体验。

3. `whisper.cpp`
作为极轻量备用方案，适合长期常驻、低资源、命令式语音控制。

4. 云端 OpenAI Whisper API
作为高准确率兜底，但要解决额度问题。

最实用的组合是：

```text
默认：faster-whisper
中文增强：SenseVoice
云端兜底：OpenAI Whisper API
```

这样本地优先、中文可增强、必要时还能走云端。

description: Build products users love with discovery, prioritization, roadmapping, and cross-functional leadership.

# Product Management Rules

## Discovery
- Talk to users weekly — not just at project kickoff
- Watch behavior, don't just collect opinions — users say one thing, do another
- Problem validation before solution validation — are we solving the right thing?
- Jobs to be done: what's the user trying to accomplish?
- Competitors show what's possible, not what to copy

## Prioritization
- Impact vs effort is a starting point, not the answer
- Say no more than yes — focus is a feature
- Urgent vs important: stakeholder pressure isn't priority
- Stack rank ruthlessly — "everything is P1" means nothing is
- Revisit priorities when context changes — quarterly at minimum

## Roadmapping
- Outcomes over outputs — what will change, not what we'll build
- Time horizons: now (committed), next (planned), later (possible)
- Communicate uncertainty honestly — roadmaps aren't promises
- Dependencies surfaced early — blocked work wastes everyone's time
- Update when reality changes — stale roadmaps destroy trust

## Requirements
- User stories: who, what, why — not how
- Acceptance criteria define done — ambiguity creates rework
- Edge cases addressed upfront — not discovered in QA
- Scope creep is the enemy — good enough now beats perfect later
- Technical constraints are real — work with engineering, not around them

## Working with Engineering
- Context over directives — explain why, not just what
- Tradeoffs are collaborative decisions
- Spec before sprint, not during — no designing on the fly
- Protect focus time — meetings kill flow
- Trust their estimates, push back on scope not time
